title: Launch review quiz
fullTitle: Launch Review Quiz: Five Questions Your Demo Can't Answer

scenes.narration: Five questions from the launch review your demo never shows. Each answer comes from a real test result in the Web Reality Checks repository. Question, three options, six seconds to think, then the answer.
captions: Five questions from the launch review your demo never shows.
Each answer comes from a real test result in the repository.

scenes.narration: Question one. Trust and access. Alice is signed in and asks for Bob's private project. In the flawed version of the app, what does the server answer? A: an error, access refused. B: Bob's project, status two hundred. Or C: not found.
captions: Question 1. Trust and access.
Alice is signed in and asks for Bob's private project.
In the flawed version, what does the server answer?

scenes.narration: The answer is B. The server checked that Alice was signed in, never that the project was hers. After the repair, the same request returns four oh four.
captions: B: Bob's project, status 200.
The server never checked who owns the project.

scenes.narration: Question two. Duplicates. A customer clicks Pay once. The server saves the order, but the confirmation is lost, so the app tries again. In the flawed version, how many orders exist? A: one. B: two. Or C: three.
captions: Question 2. Duplicates.
One click, a lost confirmation, an automatic retry.
In the flawed version, how many orders exist?

scenes.narration: B, two. Nothing linked the retry to the first request. With a unique key per purchase, the repaired version ends with one order.
captions: B: two orders.
With a unique key per purchase, the repair ends with one.

scenes.narration: Question three. Data lifecycle. A directory advertises ten thousand listings. Its checker records three thousand, eight hundred seventy-five problems. How many different listings were flagged? A: three thousand, eight hundred seventy-five. B: three thousand, three hundred three. Or C: six thousand, six hundred ninety-seven.
captions: Question 3. Data lifecycle.
10,000 listings, 3,875 problems recorded.
How many different listings were flagged?

scenes.narration: B, three thousand, three hundred three. Some listings carry several flags, so problems and affected listings are different counts. Ask which one a report shows.
captions: B: 3,303 distinct listings.
Some listings carry several flags. Ask which count a report shows.

scenes.narration: Question four. Freshness. A dashboard shows a green Live label, updated zero seconds ago. Its sensor is sampled every six hundred seconds. Just before the next sample, how old is the reading? A: zero seconds. B: thirty seconds. Or C: five hundred seventy seconds.
captions: Question 4. Freshness.
A green Live label, "updated 0 s ago". The sensor samples every 600 s.
Just before the next sample, how old is the reading?

scenes.narration: C, five hundred seventy seconds, nearly ten minutes. The label described the page refresh, not the measurement. Ask for the age of the data itself.
captions: C: 570 seconds, nearly ten minutes.
The label described the page refresh, not the measurement.

scenes.narration: Question five. Experience and speed. Eight keystrokes in a search box sent seventeen requests in the flawed version, twelve of them rejected. After the repair, how many requests for the same typing? A: eight. B: four. Or C: one.
captions: Question 5. Experience and speed.
Flawed: 8 keystrokes, 17 requests, 12 rejected.
After the repair, how many requests for the same typing?

scenes.narration: C, one. The repaired client waits for typing to pause, ignores stale answers, and respects the retry delay.
captions: C: one request.
It waits for typing to pause and respects the retry delay.

scenes.narration: That is the launch review in miniature: ask for the test, not the demo. The ten questions and every fixture are in the repository, linked below. Synthetic fixtures, not an audit or certification.
captions: Ask for the test, not the demo.
Ten questions and every fixture: the repository, linked below.
